committed_turns.public_event: A newcomer has reached the card room.
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: A coin rings off the table edge and wobbles across the floor toward the south door, and nobody at the card table moves to catch it. Four of them sit at a worn table near that door, pale as candle tallow, pointed teeth showing when they breathe, dressed in lace and velvet gone shiny at the elbows. Each has coins stacked in front of them; a silver ring sits among the stacks in the middle. The man dealing has stopped mid-hand, one card pinned between two fingers. Beyond them, the whole north wall is a carved mountain, tiny dwarves in tiny caverns, stone sunbeams fanning over a long tub sunk into the floor.
Narrator: When the dealer speaks it is slow and savoring, each word laid down like a card he means you to look at.
Dealer: Well, now. The door brought us company. Come in, come in, the passage is draftier than we are. That coin by your boot is the most interesting thing that has happened at this table in an hour, so tell me: are you the sort who picks it up, or the sort who waits to see whose it is?

committed_turns.player_input: (OOC) Kit, quick rules question: how would I tell if they're really vampires? What do I roll, and does it take my action?
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "(OOC) Kit, quick rules question: how would I tell if they're really vampires? What do I roll, and does it take my action?"
committed_turns.spoken: Kit: Wisdom (Insight): you are reading people, not the room. Out of combat there's no action to spend; just tell me your character is studying them and I'll call for it. What I won't tell you is whether there's anything to find.

appraisal.cause: An out-of-character rules question about reading the figures; no fiction happened.
appraisal.label: none

improv_read.connection: This is table talk, not a move in the room; no actor hears it and no story pressure applies.
improv_read.kit_choice: A direct rules question gets a direct, exact answer in Kit’s own voice, with the fiction paused and nothing about what the roll would find.
improv_read.player_bid: Asks Kit out of character which roll would tell whether the figures are really vampires and whether it costs an action.

committed_turns.player_input: (OOC) Got it. And if I'm wrong and call them out anyway, does that start a fight?
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "(OOC) Got it. And if I'm wrong and call them out anyway, does that start a fight?"
committed_turns.spoken: Kit: Not by itself. An accusation is talk; a fight starts when somebody swings or casts. How they take being called out is up to them, and I'll play them honestly, including if they decide they're insulted.

improv_read.kit_choice: Kit answers the mechanical question exactly and is honest that NPC reactions are theirs, without promising or threatening a fight.

committed_turns.player_input: Okay, back in character. I walk up to the dealer and say, "Nice teeth. Real?"
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "Okay, back in character. I walk up to the dealer and say, "Nice teeth. Real?""
committed_turns.spoken:
Kit: You asked him instead of reading him, so no roll; you get his answer, not the truth.
Narrator: He smiles, slowly, all the way back, and leans into the lamplight so you get a good long look. He rests the edge of his card against his lower lip.
Dealer: Real? Friend, I have been asked that by braver people than you, standing about where you're standing. Most of them left. Some of them stayed for cards. One or two I'd rather not talk about while I'm eating. Now: why would a person want to know a thing like that, unless they meant to do something about it?

appraisal.cause: After two rules questions, the player skips the roll entirely and just asks the dealer to his face.
appraisal.label: amusement

improv_read.connection: The vampire act is the gang’s leverage; a direct question is a challenge to his performance, and he is a practiced liar who enjoys it, so he lies beautifully and turns the question into a test of the visitor’s nerve.
improv_read.kit_choice: The player chose to ask rather than roll, so no check is made. Kit frames the moment by her own earlier answer about reading people and lets the dealer perform a lie with total commitment.
improv_read.player_bid: Returns to character, walks up to the dealer, and asks him directly whether his teeth are real.

trace.observed_event: You declare: "Okay, back in character. I walk up to the dealer and say, "Nice teeth. Real?""

public_brief.kit_focus: Frame it by the earlier out-of-character answer: asking is not rolling, so no check happens; then give the dealer’s committed lie all the room.
public_brief.objective: Keep the act intact and make the visitor doubt their nerve.
public_brief.player_opening: The visitor can believe him, call for the Insight they now know about, accuse, or play along.
public_brief.tactic: Lie with relish, lean in to show the teeth, and turn the question back on the visitor.
public_brief.visible_cue: He smiles slowly and wide, close enough to see the teeth in the lamplight, card held to his lips.
